subject: Post-demo: Model parity thresholds & experiment plan for PayFlux fraud workflow
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@payflux.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@payflux.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Model parity thresholds & experiment plan for PayFlux fraud workflow

Hi Emma / Oliver —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick written recap plus a lightweight experiment proposal so your security and data teams have something concrete to review.

Summary from the call
- Goal: Replace current proprietary reranker for PayFlux fraud-case triage while matching or improving on precision at top-3 and reducing token cost per decision.
- Constraint: P95 inference latency target <= 250ms for 512-token average context in prod.
- Risk area called out: hallucination/false-action suggestions are high impact — tolerance is low.

Recommended experiment plan (2-week pilot)
1) Models to trial (hosted via Redwood):
   - Open candidates: Mistral-7B-chat (float16), LlamaX-13B-Quant (int8/ptq)
   - Redwood baseline: redwood-prop-7.2B (production-tuned)
2) Acceptance thresholds (pass/fail gates):
   - Top-3 precision >= 93% (based on your 4k labeled cases)
   - Hallucination/unsafe action rate <= 1.5% (QA sample)
   - P95 latency <= 250ms (observed under realistic concurrency)
   - Unit token cost <= 0.55x of current baseline (aim to reduce cost)
3) Data & prompts
   - We will run evaluations on your 4,000 labeled fraud triage examples.
   - We'll test the prompt_set_v1 (attached) plus two conservative safety prompt wrappers to reduce actionable hallucinations.
4) Metrics & deliverables
   - Benchmarks CSV (attached) + Redwood bench dashboard link.
   - Short exec summary with recommendation and canonical prompt(s).

Security & compliance notes
- Pilot will run in Redwood Hosted Private tenancy with audit logs enabled; we can also run in your VPC if you prefer.

Next steps (proposed)
- You: confirm dataset delivery method (S3 link or Secure Drive) by Tue 5/18.
- We: run baseline + open candidates on a 2k stratified subset and deliver results by Fri 5/28.
- Sync: 30-min check-in week of 5/31 to review preliminary numbers.

Attachments: payflux_benchmark_v1.csv (sample metrics), payflux_promptset_v1.json (prompts + safety wrappers), SOW_redwood_payflux_draft.pdf (pilot scope & pricing)

If that plan looks good I’ll send a short SOW + intake checklist to your security team.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emma Liu <emma@payflux.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@payflux.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model parity thresholds & experiment plan for PayFlux fraud workflow

Thanks Aditya — that looks thorough and reasonable. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Data residency: our security team prefers the pilot run inside a customer-managed VPC (GCP region us-central1). Can Redwood spin up the private control plane there?
2) Regression detection: how will you surface quality regressions compared to our current reranker? We need an automated alert if false-action rate climbs >0.5% relative to baseline during rollout.

Also looping in Oliver (fraud ops) who will own labeling and QA. He has some questions about the acceptance threshold — 93% top-3 precision might be aggressive for certain merchant categories; can we stratify acceptance by risk tier?

Emma Liu
Head of Fraud Ops, PayFlux
emma@payflux.com

Hi Emma —

Quick answers to the two asks.

1) VPC/private control plane: yes, we can provision Redwood Private in your GCP us-central1 region for the pilot. That will keep data egress under your tenancy and give you KMS/HSM integration. I’ll include the provisioning checklist in the intake doc.

2) Regression monitoring: we’ll instrument an automated regression detector that compares rolling-window FP/false-action rate against your current reranker baseline. Alerts can be configured with a relative delta threshold (e.g., 0.5%) and routed to PagerDuty + Slack channel. We also produce daily QA digests with sampled failures and prediction context.

Regarding stratified thresholds: happy to make acceptance criteria per risk tier. Proposed initial split:
- Tier A (high-value merchants): top-3 precision >= 95%
- Tier B: >= 93%
- Tier C (low-risk): >= 90%

I’m attaching the prompt set and a short README with the safety wrappers we’ll apply. The prompt wrappers are intentionally conservative for actions that could cause money movement or account blocking.

Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
